## BK-65: Pilot privately owned photo evidence with bounded storage controls

**Evidence:** Observations store up to 12 screened photo URLs and display outbound links; no upload, attachment store, ownership/rights receipt, metadata-stripping or thumbnail lifecycle is implemented. Core v1 explicitly avoids copying images into research packages.

**Problem:** A researcher may want durable evidence from their own photographs rather than an external link, but this introduces a new private binary-data and retention boundary.

**Proposed PR:** Only after owner threat-model/rights approval, pilot authenticated upload of owned/authorized images with strict byte/type/dimension limits, safe decoding/re-encoding, explicit metadata policy, checksums and attachment-to-observation/claim references. Include attachment manifests in backup/restore/retention qualification before enabling normal use.

**Scope Boundaries:** No arbitrary URL fetching, SVG/HTML uploads, public gallery, OCR/face recognition or implied ownership of third-party linked photos. Use an established image library; never trust extension/MIME alone or assume metadata removal proves anonymity.

**Acceptance Target:** Spoofed/oversized/decompression-heavy fixtures fail boundedly; unauthenticated access is blocked; metadata policy is verified against canaries; original-versus-derived retention is explicit; restore and approved deletion include bytes/thumbnails/references without orphaning provenance.

**Dependencies:** BK-19, BK-26, BK-42, BK-49. **Classification:** Stretch, Evidence Storage, Security, Privacy. **Priority:** P4.

**Distinct From:** BK-24/32 distribute selected text/data; this introduces a deliberately separate private owned-image evidence subsystem.

**Evidence:** Current basemaps are present-day remote tiles; BK-31 proposes sourced historical relations/time layers and optional footprints. Archival citation locators and explicit uncertainty can support a narrowly reviewed historical map-image comparison, but no raster ingest/calibration workflow exists.

**Proposed PR:** Pilot one owner-approved licensed raster with original archive/rights metadata, dated interpretation, selected control points, a declared transform and residual/error receipt. ## BK-61: Replay seeded action sequences against trust and provenance invariants

**Evidence:** Existing tests cover individual imports, edits, merges, observation idempotency and route revalidation. Their interactions depend on revisions, retained historical items, merged identities and repeated migrations; examples alone do not exhaust ordered combinations.

**Problem:** A regression can appear only after a valid sequence such as import, review, corrected observation, merge, repeated import and stale route lookup.

**Proposed PR:** Add a bounded deterministic sequence generator using the existing synthetic fixtures and stdlib seeded randomness. Define independent invariants for candidate-only imports, revision monotonicity, immutable payloads, evidence identity, protected reviewed fields and invalid route eligibility. Retain seed/action trace and reduce a failing trace to a small regression case.

**Scope Boundaries:** No new fuzzing framework, huge nightly corpus or using the production catalogue. Do not derive the oracle entirely from the function under test; a passing sequence suite is engineering proof, not historical truth.

**Acceptance Target:** Fixed seeds replay identically; injected guard/hash/evidence regressions are detected; shortened failing traces become ordinary tests; a declared bounded CI runtime is measured before expanding the corpus.

**Dependencies:** BK-02, BK-04, BK-14, BK-19, BK-38. **Classification:** Testing, Reliability, Core Domain. **Priority:** P2.

**Distinct From:** BK-11 diagnoses browser timing and BK-29 measures scale; this qualifies API/domain behavior across action sequences.

## BK-60: Reconcile new seed content against persistent curator overrides

**Evidence:** Main enrichment is bundled JSON, while the editor branch uses override-first persisted `content_json` with seed fallback. BK-12 preserves current seed data during integration; it does not define what happens when a later release changes a claim underneath an older override.

**Problem:** A full override can keep useful newer source content invisible, while blindly replacing it could erase deliberate local curation.

**Proposed PR:** Record the seed version/hash an override was based on and compare base/current seed/local override by stable claim/source IDs. Present a three-way reconciliation draft with explicit unchanged/new/conflicting/removed cases, allowing the curator to retain or adopt individual changes through normal revisioned editing.

**Scope Boundaries:** No automatic text merge, repinning to hide drift, silent deletion of unused sources or modification of trust/access during code deployment. Legacy overrides without a known base are labeled and reviewed conservatively.

**Acceptance Target:** Disjoint new seed claims are visible as proposals, conflicting local edits stay intact, removed referenced sources require a decision, and failed reconciliation preserves the original override; receipt identifies reviewed versions and resulting revision.

**Dependencies:** BK-12, BK-35, BK-46. **Classification:** Product, Reliability, Content Operations. **Priority:** P2.

## BK-58: Capture opt-in observation fixes without inventing feature accuracy

**Evidence:** `getCurrentPosition` is currently opt-in for route start and displays instrument accuracy; observation forms require manual coordinates, point role and radius. The code correctly does not treat browser position as a feature observation.

**Problem:** Recording a public-viewpoint observation can require manual coordinate transfer, but reusing GPS carelessly would collapse observer position, instrument accuracy and actual feature uncertainty.

**Proposed PR:** Add an explicit one-shot capture into an observation draft, storing measurement timestamp/age and reported instrument accuracy separately from curator-declared feature uncertainty. ## BK-52: Navigate a private source registry across linked sites and claims
